chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man sets out for the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), upon taking his first step from his home, his sins are forgiven. He continues to be purified with every step until he arrives. When he reaches it, Allah converses with him and says: 'O My servant, ask of Me and I will give you; call upon Me and I will answer you; seek from Me and I will give you; ask Me for your need and I will fulfill it for you.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: And it is incumbent upon Allah to give what was spent (by the pilgrim).

key_terms.أَقْضِهَا لَکَ: I will fulfill it for you

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and divine promises for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the metaphysical reality of Ziyarat as a journey of progressive sanctification, where the physical act of walking transforms into spiritual purification. This narrative underscores the concept of 'Haqq al-Allah' (Allah's obligation) to reward the pilgrim, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory power and spiritual proximity of the Imams. The personal dialogue between Allah and the pilgrim emphasizes the intimate accessibility of the Divine through the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.).
